questions.q: What does a Roll-Up Summary field calculate from, that a Formula field does not?
options: A set of related child records, instead of just fields on its own record
Values typed directly by the user
Nothing — the two field types are identical
questions.explain: A Formula field calculates from fields on its own record; a Roll-Up Summary field aggregates values from a whole set of related detail (child) records.

questions.q: Which relationship type do Roll-Up Summary fields rely on, per Salesforce's own documentation?
questions.explain: Roll-Up Summary fields are defined on the master object of a master-detail relationship, summarizing records on the detail side.

questions.q: Which summary type totals a numeric field across every related child record?
questions.explain: SUM totals the values in the chosen Field to Aggregate across all related detail records.

questions.q: In the lesson's real example, what two different roll-up fields were built from the exact same two Product records?
options: Two COUNT fields with different filters
A SUM (Total List Price) and a MIN (Minimum List Price)
Two SUM fields on different objects
A Formula field and a Picklist field
questions.explain: The same two Product line items fed both a SUM roll-up (Total List Price) and a MIN roll-up (Minimum List Price) — same data, different aggregate, different answer.

questions.q: Besides the summary type and the field to aggregate, what optional setting can narrow which child records a Roll-Up Summary field includes?
questions.explain: Roll-Up Summary fields support optional filter criteria, so the aggregate can include only child records matching specific conditions instead of every related record.
